title: GPU surge smoothing and atomic evictor safeguard
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Multiple customers (hosted + dedicated) reported sudden GPU OOMs during short high-throughput bursts. Investigation shows a compound failure mode: (1) asynchronous prefix/KV write backlog builds up when compaction is delayed by allocator contention; (2) the evictor cycle can skip tombstone reconciliation in an atomicity gap when an evictor heartbeat races with session handoff; (3) the allocator prefers high-water allocations causing large arena fragmentation. The combined effect produces long-tail memory spikes that exhaust GPU memory under bursty traffic.

Why this ticket exists: we need a coordinated runtime change set to (A) prevent the async-evictor atomicity gap, (B) smooth GPU burst pressure via graceful per-tenant throttle and bounded arenas, and (C) drain kvcache write queues without impacting SLOs. This is a customer escalation for two enterprise customers and multiple hosted customers experiencing degraded availability and failed inferences.

Observed signals and evidence:
- spike in evictor latency (evictor:latency p95 > 800ms) correlated with foreign-hosted batch windows
- kvcache:pending_writes consistently rising before OOM events
- allocator free-list exhaustion and large contiguous allocation failures in GPU driver logs
- stack traces show race between prefix write completion and async tombstone reclamation

Root cause hypothesis: a race condition in the evictor loop allowed a small window where tombstones were not visible to the compactor when session handoff occurs. Under heavy writes the kvcache backlog grows; the allocator then fragments arenas trying to satisfy large transient tensors. The combination crosses GPU memory thresholds and triggers OOM.

Scope: affects hosted, Dedicated capacity pools with mixed-priority tenants, and early private deploys with similar runtime versions. Not all tenants trigger the failure; multi-tenant contention and burst patterns are required.
acceptance_criteria: Evictor loop has an atomic fence preventing missed tombstones under session handoff (unit + integration tests added)
New metrics (kvcache:pending_writes, evictor:atomic_fence_misses) emit and used in dashboards
Canary rollout to 5% of runtime nodes shows reduction in p95 evictor latency and no regressions in token throughput
Graceful per-tenant GPU throttle limits reduce OOM frequency to zero in canary and allow safe rollback
Customer incidents escalated here confirm successful mitigation in their environments (hosted + dedicated customers)
steps_taken: 2025-02-12: Triage call with oncall, SE, and affected customer reps. Collected traces and Kernel logs. Created initial hypothesis (Maya Chen)
2025-02-13: Reproduced a reduced test-case in staging that triggers a similar alloc/evictor race; added debug metrics to kvcache (Arjun Patel)
2025-02-14: Implemented experimental evictor fence (sequence-number based) in a local branch; ran allocator stress tests (perf-team)
2025-02-15: Observed reduced pending_writes in local runs; however fragmentation still occurs under synthetic tensor churn. Added bounded-per-session arena patch to prevent arena runaway (Arjun)
2025-02-16: Opened PR #1298 with evictor-fence + bounded arenas + metric emissions. Tests added: unit for fence, integration reproducing race (PR link below)
2025-02-17: Deployed PR to canary pool (5% nodes) with a conservative per-tenant throttle policy; monitoring dashboard shows evictor latency drop and backlog stabilization (SRE)
2025-02-18: Two affected hosted customers confirmed reduced incidence of failed inferences during their batch windows; dedicated customer requested dedicated rollout schedule (Customer Success)
2025-02-19: Added graceful fallback to compact-on-demand when pending_writes exceeds threshold; updated rollback plan and alert thresholds (Arjun)
2025-02-20: Preparing release candidate for runtime-2025.03; scheduling 25% rollout after cross-team signoff. Postmortem draft started.
rollback_plan: If the canary shows regression (increased inference error rate or token latency > 2x baseline), immediately revert to previous runtime image, disable per-tenant throttle, and enable manual compaction loop. Slack incident channel: #incident-runtime-evictor (oncall + runtime-leads)
test_plan: Unit tests for atomic fence and bounded arenas; integration test harness that reproduces race under controlled thread scheduling; soak test for 24h on canary nodes; perf regression tests to verify token throughput impact < 5%
customer_communication: Customer-facing summary drafted and sent to CS for affected hosted customers; dedicated customer engagement scheduled 2025-02-21 to run private rollout and verify. Suggested mitigations for customers: stagger batch windows and lower burst concurrency until runtime-2025.03 is rolled out
next_steps: Complete PR feedback loop, run full 25% rollout in prod pools, finalize postmortem, backport minimal guard to maintained 2024.x branches for private deployments
